currentContext.business: Pelatro Limited is a global technology company that provides customer engagement and monetisation solutions to telecom operators and digital businesses. Its flagship mViva platform enables operators to understand subscriber behaviour and to design, execute and measure personalised, contextual engagement across the customer lifecycle; at the end of FY26 it was deployed across 46 telecom networks, processing data for approximately 1.5 billion consumers with more than 20,000 campaigns executed. Following the acquisition of the software business of Estel Technologies, the Company reorganised into two reportable segments with effect from 1 July 2025 — the CVM Division (customer value management and engagement around mViva) and the Estel Division (prepaid recharge, voucher management, sales and distribution, and mobile money platforms).

currentContext.strengths: Asset-light, platform-led, non-linear model: already-developed core software products are deployed many times across operators, networks and geographies with only minor upgradations and customisations, giving high contribution margins and significant operating leverage|Mission-critical position in an operator's commercial operations — a meaningful share of day-to-day customer interactions and revenue-generating activity runs through the platform — creating high switching costs and deep multi-year relationships|High revenue quality and visibility: repeat (recurring plus re-occurring) revenue was 82% of FY26 revenue, and approximately 82% of FY27 revenue was already contracted as at the date of reporting|Track record of customers extending deployments to additional networks and geographies within their group once the value proposition has been proven|Differentiation on domain depth, breadth of the mViva platform, proven large-scale deployments and an increasingly AI-led product roadmap versus large global vendors and specialised regional players|Broadened end-to-end proposition after the Estel Division addition, spanning customer engagement/monetisation and transaction-oriented capabilities, creating cross-sell opportunities across the combined customer base|Conservatively funded, capital-light and cash-generative balance sheet, with a consolidated debt-equity ratio of 0.12 as at 31 March 2026|Centralised, substantially remote delivery from India supported by international subsidiaries, allowing large-scale deployments to be implemented and operated cost-efficiently
currentContext.strategies: Pursue a blended strategy of organic and inorganic growth — 'Any software product company must work on a blended strategy of organic and inorganic growth', with disciplined target selection on synergy, product relevance and telecom-industry reputation, and on revenue-growth potential, profitability and ROCE|Embed AI across the product set ('AI-First' offerings) to maintain product leadership, and use AI internally to reduce cost of operation and time to market while increasing quality — reducing cost per dollar of revenue and supporting non-linearity|Integrate and scale the acquired Estel Division (completed 1 July 2025) as a second growth vertical, through productization, a continuously evolving product road map and a rebuilt sales pipeline|Cross-sell CVM and AI engagement tools into Estel customers and Estel solutions into Pelatro telecom accounts to increase wallet share per telecom operator|Position the combined business as a multi-layer, full-stack telecom monetisation and transaction platform spanning intelligence (AI/CVM), execution (recharge, wallet), infrastructure (distribution systems) and monetisation (payments + fintech)|Build non-linearity through productization — standardised offerings that reduce customer-specific development and the incremental cost of each new contract, leading to higher profitability|Deepen penetration of a large under-served market: 8 products across the two Divisions against an average of around 1.3 products per customer today, plus increasing market penetration across the roughly 450 telcos globally|The AGM notice puts to members the declaration of a final dividend of INR 1 per equity share for the financial year ended 31 March 2026, indicating a modest cash-return intent alongside retention of the balance of profits. A special resolution seeks approval for commission to the Non-Executive Director and Independent Directors of Rs. 5,50,000 each (totalling Rs. 16,50,000), which exceeds the 1% of net profits limit under Section 198 for FY26. The Company reports no applications or proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code during the year, no one-time settlement with banks or financial institutions, and no unpaid or unclaimed amounts requiring transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. An Employee Stock Option Plan 2025 was implemented during the year, approved by shareholders on 20 November 2025 via postal ballot. The Company is listed on NSE-Emerge as an SME, for which SEBI LODR corporate-governance provisions are not mandatory.
currentContext.expansion: Pelatro is an asset-light, capital-light, platform-led business: its already-developed core software products are deployed many times across multiple operators, networks and geographies with only minor upgradations and customisations, so expansion is expressed as footprint, platform build-out and acquisition rather than plant capex. The principal expansion step of FY26 was inorganic — the acquisition of the software business of Estel Technologies, effective 1 July 2025, after which the Company reorganised into two reportable segments (the CVM Division around mViva and the Estel Division covering prepaid recharge, voucher management, sales and distribution, and mobile money platforms), establishing a second growth vertical and an end-to-end telecom commercial proposition. Post-acquisition work has been integration-led: within nine months of closing the Company completed the first stage of productization and the product road map for the acquired business, and at the end of ten months from closing it had rebuilt a pipeline (Estel had almost no pipeline when acquired) that has already started yielding new contracts, with management expecting wins from that pipeline over the next 8 to 10 months. On the product side, the Company is addressing growing demand for AI-driven engagement through the launch of the mViva Revenue Acceleration Platform with Agentic AI. Reach expansion is geographic and cross-sell led: the mViva platform is deployed across 46 telecom networks (33 countries per the Company Overview; 35 countries per the MD&A), the Company targets geographic white-space in existing and adjacent emerging markets where CVM adoption and digital monetisation remain early, and it aims to raise the average of around 1.3 products per customer across its 8 products spanning the two Divisions. The model remains conservatively funded, with a consolidated debt-equity ratio of 0.12 as at 31 March 2026. The annual-report text supplied discloses no manufacturing capacity and no rupee capital-expenditure quantum.

risks.note: Revenue is derived from a focused base of telecom operators, so the loss, consolidation or financial stress of a large customer would bite; mitigation is geographic diversification, deeper engagement across the expanded product portfolio and a high share of recurring revenue.

risks.risk: Revenue variability from long, lumpy enterprise licensing cycles
risks.note: Enterprise licensing cycles can be long and uneven, causing quarter-to-quarter variability; management explicitly tracks growth year-on-year rather than sequentially because quarterly comparison is not representative given the long sales and implementation cycles. A growing recurring and re-occurring base and a strong contracted order position reduce the exposure.

The pace of change in AI and customer-engagement technology requires sustained product investment to stay competitive; the Company points to continuous innovation, illustrated by the launch of its Agentic AI platform.

A significant proportion of revenue and assets is denominated in foreign currencies, exposing the Company to currency movements; it monitors FX fluctuations closely on an ongoing basis to determine corrective steps.
The Company must integrate acquired businesses and realise expected synergies; the Estel integration progressed during the year with margin improvement targeted over the medium term.
The nature of enterprise contracts can extend collection cycles; the Company actively manages credit exposure and the timing of collections.
The business depends on skilled technology and delivery professionals; the Company invests in talent acquisition, development and retention.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk across multiple jurisdictions
risks.note: The Company operates across multiple jurisdictions and is subject to evolving legal and regulatory requirements, including data-protection and labour regulations such as the New Labour Codes notified during the year; it closely monitors regulatory change.
